content.important: Permission, hardware readiness, network reachability, and device visibility are different things. A readiness checkmark is not a safety verdict.

sections.body: Spectra requires an iPhone running iOS 27 or later. Scanning, Bluetooth Proximity, saved results, and JSON export do not require Apple Intelligence or an in-app purchase. Each measurement still needs its hardware and permission; Spectra checks selected measurements before a scan and explains anything unavailable.
sections.title: Supported iPhones

sections.body: Only on-device analysis requires an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone with Apple Intelligence enabled and ready in a supported language and region. If your iPhone does not support it, or the model is disabled or still downloading, you can still scan, review all measured evidence, and export JSON. No analysis runs automatically. Availability is checked separately when you use analysis.
sections.title: Apple Intelligence is optional

sections.body: Welcome explains the app. **Get Started** opens measurement setup. Tap a measurement to request its access; a readiness checkmark reflects the system response. You can continue without every permission. A prompt explains what remains unconfigured, and a later check requests only missing access.
sections.title: Start with access

sections.body: **Quick Check** uses Bluetooth and optional **Local network** for 30 seconds. **Area Sweep** can use Bluetooth, **Local network**, and **Motion and magnetic**, together or independently, with an extendable 30-minute limit. **Monitor** is stationary and radio-only. **Smart Glasses** and **Watches & Wearables** keep Bluetooth fixed; their short preparation screen offers the same optional **Tag location** choice as other iPhone checks. Completed results offer name search and a separate **View observed activity** route for Bluetooth identities that did not match. Device types are estimates, not selectable filters.
sections.title: Choose measurements for each check

sections.body: Touch and hold Spectra’s app icon, then choose **Quick Check**, **Smart Glasses**, or **Watches & Wearables**. **Quick Check** opens measurement selection; the specialist shortcuts open their Bluetooth-only preparation screen. Location tagging stays optional and off until you choose it. On first use, finish **Welcome** and measurement setup, then explicitly start your requested check. Canceling clears that request. If a check is still open, including its completed results, or another task is presented over the app, Spectra preserves it instead of starting another scan; close it and choose the shortcut again. Shortcuts do not enable background scanning or completion sounds.
sections.title: Start from the Home Screen

sections.body: The iPhone **Area Sweep** limit starts when collection begins, not while permissions or instructions are open. At 25 minutes, a quiet notice offers **Extend 30 Minutes** or **Finish Area Sweep**. Each extension adds 30 minutes to the deadline, with another notice five minutes before it. Elapsed time stays visible. At the deadline, Spectra finishes through its normal results flow and follows **Save completed sessions**; it does not override your saving preference. Confirm the saved status or use **Retry Saving** or **Export JSON** if needed. **Monitor** and the Watch’s 30-second sweep are unchanged. Longer listening does not guarantee complete discovery or unlimited retained evidence.
sections.title: Take your time, with a clear stopping point

sections.body: Before any iPhone check, optionally turn on **Tag location**. It is off for each new check and asks for Location access only when chosen. Approximate access is supported; scanning still works if permission is denied or a usable fix is unavailable. Spectra requests a single position near collection start and stops requesting it after a short window. **Scan start location** shows coordinates and estimated accuracy, not an address, route, room, or detected-device position. You can separately enable automatic map previews of saved areas through Apple Maps; this does not request your current location. Watch captures do not receive the phone’s location when imported. Location is not required for Bluetooth, local-network, or magnetic measurements.
sections.title: Remember where a check began

sections.body: In Spectra, open **Settings** → **App icon** to choose **Classic**, **Spectra Blue**, **Light**, or **Blue on White**. Each uses Spectra’s original waveform. A checkmark identifies the icon confirmed by iOS; a spinner shows a change in progress. This changes the app icon, not the colors inside Spectra. Your iPhone’s icon appearance settings may adjust the colors. **Reset Spectra** erases local data and returns to **Welcome** first, then asks iOS to restore **Classic**. If iOS takes longer than expected, Spectra reports the unconfirmed change; iOS may still finish an earlier request. Review the icon in **Settings** after setup.
sections.title: Choose an app icon

sections.body: Local Network needs a joined Wi-Fi or supported wired local link and permission. Spectra offers **Check again** when readiness can be rechecked, or continuation without that measurement when others can run. Returning from **Settings** rechecks availability; it does not silently start a scan. An internet connection is not required for local discovery.
sections.title: No local network available?

sections.body: A completed source ran for the available check window, not that every device was found. **Partial** means coverage was interrupted or quality-limited. **Unavailable** means the source could not run; **Not selected** means you excluded it. Read the accompanying reason before drawing conclusions. **Observation handling** counts are not physical-device counts or available disk space.
sections.title: Read Coverage

steps: In Spectra, open **Settings** → **Privacy & storage** → **Measurement access** to review permissions and sensor readiness. Tap **Done** to return; unused measurements do not need to be configured.

For **Access not allowed**, change Spectra’s access in iPhone **Settings**, then return to Spectra for a fresh access check. Retrying cannot add unsupported hardware or override an iOS restriction; follow its guidance or choose different measurements.
Return to Spectra, choose measurements, and review any readiness message before starting.
content.takeaway: Allow only the measurements you want. Setup prepares access; it does not start a scan.

technicalSections.body: Showing an optional Wi-Fi name uses Apple’s Access Wi-Fi Information rules, including Precise Location While Using the App when required. This is not needed for Bluetooth, magnetic exploration, or Bonjour browsing. The Wi-Fi-name action does not request geographic coordinates or save the name. **Tag location** is a separate, per-check request for coordinates; granting permission alone does not enable it. iOS may withhold a Wi-Fi name even when local discovery can operate.
technicalSections.title: Why does Wi-Fi name ask for Location?

technicalSections.body: Spectra accepts a fix at most ten seconds old and waits up to twelve seconds from collection start. A fix must report estimated horizontal accuracy of 5 km or better. Approximate permission can produce a broad region, and indoor reception may yield no usable fix. These are freshness and quality bounds, not a guarantee of accuracy. No automatic address lookup is performed. If no fix qualifies, the check continues without a tag. Starting another check never reuses a prior session’s position as its own.
technicalSections.title: When can a location tag be saved?

technicalSections.body: The displayed network name provides connection context, not a router model, physical location, or assurance that the network is trustworthy. Guest networks and client isolation may prevent discovering other clients despite a working connection.
technicalSections.title: A Wi-Fi name is not a router identity

technicalSections.body: **Bluetooth Proximity** listens for new broadcasts. A private reference retained with a new iPhone capture can recognize the original framework identity after reopening; it cannot make a silent or rotating advertiser appear. Older or imported sessions and Watch captures may need a confirmed possible match. If no useful name or supported payload clue was retained and no private reference is available, Spectra explains that limitation rather than starting an indistinguishable search. Bluetooth access and finding the signal are separate requirements. A saved signal strength is not a current reading.
technicalSections.title: Why is a saved signal not available?

technicalSections.body: Spectra uses a fixed standard text size. Changing iOS Dynamic Type or Larger Text does not resize the app’s own interface. VoiceOver labels remain available, and contrast and reduced-motion preferences still apply. System-owned permission dialogs and sharing interfaces are controlled by iOS.
technicalSections.title: Text size and accessibility

technicalSections.body: The shipped device catalog, Guide, Bluetooth observation, magnetic exploration, saved history, and preparing JSON work on device. Apple Intelligence analysis also works locally once its supported model is ready. Local Network still needs a usable local link. Loading a map preview, sending email, opening website help, cloud file destinations, or using an external AI service may require internet. An unavailable map does not prevent reviewing saved coordinates or findings.
technicalSections.title: What works without internet?

content.title: Set up measurements and permissions

content.important: An observation does not prove that a device is recording or malicious. A quiet check cannot prove that a space is clear.

sections.body: Spectra reads broadcasts, advertised network services, and iPhone sensor measurements. It does not pair with or open sessions to discovered devices.
sections.title: Observe without connecting

sections.body: We regularly improve Spectra’s device catalog and detection engine to help you make better sense of nearby signals. These improvements are included in app updates at no additional charge. Install updates through the App Store; there is no separate catalog download or subscription. Newer recognition can also help you revisit eligible saved sessions with **Recheck session**, without changing the original. An update does not guarantee a match or make every device detectable.
sections.title: Built to keep getting better

sections.body: **Summary** surfaces named findings and supported possible device types, even when the manufacturer or model is unknown. Each result keeps its confidence or name-source label. Related observations stay together; other unnamed activity stays compact. Expand a result for its measurements and supporting evidence.
sections.title: Start with the summary

sections.body: Local-network discovery can reveal supported printing, scanning, file sharing, media, automation, and imaging or audio services. A service describes what an endpoint advertises, not necessarily a physical device: a computer can host a print queue, and an imaging service may also belong to audio hardware. Reviewed names and protocol-specific model fields can support a **Possible** product or family. Without those clues, Spectra keeps the service role and its uncertainty visible instead of inventing a model.
sections.title: Recognize a network role without an exact device

sections.body: A **Possible smartwatch** or **Possible audio output** can appear without a product name when reviewed broadcast evidence supports that category. A result shows up to three retained possible interpretations; **Technical details** holds the remaining retained interpretations and their sources. These possibilities are not an exhaustive list of products. The **Conflicting identity claims** label means Spectra has not selected a product. Multiple interpretations do not create extra devices or increase review priority. The same eligible finding stays available for **Bluetooth Proximity** and analysis; neither verifies its identity.
sections.title: A useful clue without an exact model

sections.body: Choose **Smart Glasses** or **Watches & Wearables** from **Specialist checks** for a 30-second Bluetooth observation. **Watches & Wearables** includes supported smartwatches, fitness bands and trackers, smart rings, and other wearables; glasses stay in their own check. Results include catalog matches, reviewed possible category evidence, and explicitly **Possible** indications from names such as Smart Watch, Smart Ring, Fitness Tracker, or Smart Frames. Names do not establish a manufacturer or model. Names without a supported type, accessories, generic services, and company codes alone do not qualify. Spectra cannot tell whether a microphone, camera, or conversation-summary feature is active.
sections.title: Check for glasses or wearables

sections.body: During a wearable check, the overview counts findings by type. Repeated broadcasts from the same retained Bluetooth identity count once; rotating identities can still represent one physical device. After completion, **Search names** finds a particular supported match without changing the type counts. Device types are estimates, not selectable filters. **View observed activity** opens every other retained Bluetooth identity, including names whose type could not be determined. This separate context is not a specialist match and is excluded from specialist export, analysis, and proximity choices. Export, on-device analysis choices, and **Bluetooth Proximity** still include every eligible finding in the check, regardless of the display filters. Older sessions without a recorded wearable subtype appear under **Other wearables** without changing their saved product interpretation.
sections.title: Understand the wearable overview

sections.body: **Monitor** compares Bluetooth and local-network observations with a starting baseline while your iPhone stays in one place. The dashboard retains new, returned, and no-longer-recent observations. Choose **Stop Monitor** to review details. Rotating or intermittent broadcasts can cause changes without a device arriving or leaving. Magnetic exploration belongs in **Area Sweep**.
sections.title: Watch for radio changes

steps: Choose a 30-second radio **Quick Check**, a self-paced **Area Sweep** with an extendable 30-minute limit, or **Monitor** to watch one area.

Choose measurements; Quick Check records every supported category. Filter completed results by recorded measurement or search names, or use a Bluetooth-only specialist check. Keep Spectra visible while scanning.
Review what stood out, then open **Coverage** to see what was—and was not—measured.
content.takeaway: Spectra helps you investigate nearby signals. A signal is a clue—not proof of a hidden device.

technicalSections.body: Product-family labels come from reviewed metadata and an offline catalog. **Possible**, **Probable**, and signature labels describe the evidence—not numeric probabilities. A **System name** comes from the collecting device’s Bluetooth framework and may be cached rather than transmitted in that observation. Names and payloads can be changed or spoofed.
technicalSections.title: Names are claims, not authentication

technicalSections.body: Bluetooth company codes and member service numbers identify registered namespaces, sometimes belonging to a chip or protocol provider. **Google-registered Bluetooth service**, for example, means Google registered that service code—not that Google made the nearby device. **Device unknown** means Spectra has not identified the device. This is not an account-registration message or evidence that the device is communicating with Google. **Technical details** retain the service codes, parser outcomes, sources and registry versions. A **Registry model** uses a public Matter vendor/product record matched to unverified broadcast identifiers; it does not prove the hardware is genuine. Saved catalog and name-based interpretations remain recorded history. An eligible session can be explicitly rechecked with newer recognition, creating a separate copy without changing the original.
technicalSections.title: Registry context is not a verified maker

technicalSections.body: Reviewed complete broadcasts can reveal a protocol or declared category without an exact product. **Nearby Presence broadcast** describes a public proximity-related format, not a particular phone or wearable. **Possible phone · Nearby sharing broadcast** means the reviewed sharing format declares a phone category; it does not identify a maker, model, owner or operating system. **Possible HomeKit camera** is an accessory-category claim, not proof that Apple made the device or that it is recording. Supported audio formats can suggest an audio accessory. These clues are unauthenticated and may be spoofed. Unknown or incomplete formats stay uninterpreted. Encrypted contents and account information stay opaque; rotating identifiers are not resolved into an owner or stable device identity.
technicalSections.title: Useful clues inside a broadcast

technicalSections.body: Some complete broadcasts contain public product codes. Spectra can look up a Matter vendor/product tuple in its bundled public registry, or a supported MiBeacon product code in a reviewed model table. A public outer-header code may still be usable when the contents are encrypted; Spectra does not decrypt them. A **Possible** model or device type is a clue, not authenticated hardware. Supported sensor and automation formats may identify a family without a specific model. A code’s registered owner or ecosystem is not automatically the device’s manufacturer. Conflicting claims remain alternatives; saved findings retain the interpretation from that session until you explicitly recheck an eligible copy.
technicalSections.title: Model clues without a broadcast name

technicalSections.body: **Weave setup advertisement**, **Bluetooth Mesh setup advertisement**, **Bluetooth Mesh proxy advertisement**, and **AltBeacon proximity broadcast** describe supported public formats, not a product, physical device type, owner, or activity. Weave vendor/product codes use their own namespace, not the Matter registry. Private identifiers and security-state details are not exposed as recognition clues. A complete **Technical archive** can still contain their raw bytes; review it before sharing.
technicalSections.title: A protocol without a device type

technicalSections.body: Reviewed product and family names help identify both Bluetooth and local-network observations. A recognizable Apple TV name, for example, can suggest the same family on either source. Protocol-specific model fields and byte signatures still require the matching protocol evidence. Bluetooth-only name decorations such as LE are not removed from ordinary network names. Sharing catalog knowledge does not merge the observations into one physical device or raise their confidence. A shared name, manufacturer, strength, or timing cannot establish that relationship. Magnetic observations are area clues, not device identities.
technicalSections.title: Shared knowledge, separate observations

content.title: How detection works

content.important: For a credible threat or highly sensitive activity, do not rely on a phone scan. Move sensitive conversations to a more appropriate location and consult a trusted security contact. Do not tamper with equipment or confront people based on an app result.

sections.body: At a hotel, Airbnb or other vacation rental, or in student housing, start with a **Quick Check** to get oriented. Use **Area Sweep** for a closer, unhurried look at accessible areas you are allowed to inspect. In gyms and changing rooms, respect other people's privacy and facility rules; move to a private place to review findings. An unfamiliar broadcast is not evidence of covert recording, and a signal may come from outside the room.
sections.title: Hotels, rentals, and shared spaces

sections.body: As a passenger, or while waiting in an airport, station, café, or other public space, a **Quick Check** can provide a snapshot of available signals. Specialist checks focus on recognizable glasses or wearables. Crowds contain many ordinary devices; names and signal strength cannot identify the person carrying one. Do not scan while driving or confront someone based on a result.
sections.title: Rideshares and busy public places

sections.body: Review partial or unavailable sources before interpreting results. A 30-second snapshot can miss intermittent broadcasts. Local Network reaches only visible services on your joined network.
sections.title: Check what was actually measured

sections.body: A product name can be changed or spoofed. Strong Bluetooth readings are not distance, and magnetic spikes can come from ordinary magnets or wiring. Neither identifies recording activity. Clear measurement filters and name search to include every retained result. In specialist checks, also open **View observed activity**; an unidentified device may not appear among supported matches.
sections.title: Separate clues from conclusions

sections.body: Confirm the intended Wi-Fi name with the venue using a trusted channel; a familiar name alone does not authenticate a network. Prefer cellular data when you do not trust the connection. Keep iOS and apps updated, protect accounts with multifactor authentication, and heed certificate warnings. HTTPS protects traffic to a site but does not prove that the site itself is trustworthy. Avoid exposing sensitive conversations or screens in shared spaces.
sections.title: Protect the connection, too

sections.body: If you use shared Wi-Fi, consider a reputable VPN you trust and can use under your organization's policy. It encrypts traffic routed through its tunnel between your phone and the VPN service; trust shifts to that provider. It does not prevent nearby cameras or microphones from recording, authenticate a hotspot, make you anonymous, or make a malicious website safe. Spectra does not provide a VPN. VPN settings can affect local-network discovery; do not turn off required protection just to find more devices.
sections.title: Where a VPN helps—and where it does not

sections.body: Rename a saved session and add notes about areas inspected, repeatable changes, alternative explanations, and unresolved questions. Notes are yours, not sensor evidence. Avoid sensitive itinerary or personal details.
sections.title: Record the context

steps: Choose **Quick Check** for a radio snapshot or **Area Sweep** for deliberate exploration. Do not join an unfamiliar Wi-Fi network just to scan.
Review coverage, repeat observations from consistent positions, and consider ordinary explanations before escalating.
Check unclassified and out-of-filter results. **Expected** is your label for this check, not authenticated safety.
Confirm saving before closing; use **Sessions** to add your context. An earlier check does not describe the space now.
content.takeaway: Use Spectra to inform your next decision—not to certify that a space is safe.

technicalSections.body: Reports and notes are bounded local records, not authenticated exports or a forensic chain of custody. The primary history file keeps at most **500 sessions** within **256 MiB**. Saved sessions are not automatically removed; export and delete copies you no longer need to make room. A matching archive checksum does not authenticate its author, collector, or contents. Temporary replacement files and protected recovery copies may use additional disk space. Spectra marks local history for exclusion from device backups; iOS controls backup and restore behavior. Files you export may be backed up by your chosen destination.
technicalSections.title: Not a forensic record

technicalSections.body: Silent, wired, shielded, powered-off, or unrecognizable devices can remain invisible. Identity rotation can produce more than one exact record, and the app does not merge devices across sessions. No checklist or result is an all-clear.
technicalSections.title: Beyond the iPhone's visibility

content.title: Reviewing an unfamiliar space

content.important: **Experimental** means behavior is still being validated across Watches and environments. Bluetooth identifiers are not a verified device count. An empty or partial capture is never an all-clear.

sections.body: The optional Experimental Watch companion requires watchOS 27 or later and a paired iPhone running iOS 27 or later with Spectra. The iPhone app works without an Apple Watch. The companion offers only a 30-second Bluetooth **Area Sweep**. It does not measure local-network services or magnetic fields, run specialist checks, tag locations, or identify devices on the Watch. New captures transfer automatically to your paired iPhone, where Spectra identifies retained signals and saves the result in **Sessions**. Importing does not attach the phone’s current location.
sections.title: One check, a smaller screen

sections.body: After installing the companion and opening Spectra on your paired iPhone once to prepare transfer, you can collect without your iPhone nearby. The Watch uses its own Bluetooth radio and saves captures locally; collection does not need an internet connection or cellular plan. Keep Bluetooth available, allow access, and keep Spectra active with the display fully awake for each 30-second sweep. Check **Saved sweeps** before heading out: the Watch holds up to five captures in total, including earlier copies. When you reconnect, open Spectra on your paired iPhone to identify signals and review findings in **Sessions**. The Watch shows capture and transfer status, not identified results.
sections.title: Leave your iPhone behind, review later

sections.body: The Watch start screen keeps **Start Sweep** as the main action. The tray button opens **Saved sweeps** for captures and transfer status. Open **Settings** below **Start Sweep** for **Sweep guidance**, **Storage & transfer**, **Diagnostic reports**, and **About**. **About** shows the version, release identifier, numeric build and watchOS version installed on your Watch; check these separately from iPhone when troubleshooting an update. Recognition uses the engine and catalog installed on iPhone, not a separate Watch catalog.
sections.title: A focused start, help when you need it

sections.body: **Completion haptic** in Spectra’s Watch **Settings** is on by default. Turn it off if you prefer visual feedback only. The system feedback follows your Watch sound and haptic settings; it is not a guarantee of silent operation. Read the completion or partial-capture status: feedback alone does not mean that every nearby device was observed or that transfer finished.
sections.title: Choose completion feedback

sections.body: On Apple Watch, open **Settings** → **Display & Brightness** → **Wake Duration** and choose **Wake for 70 Seconds**. Tap to wake the display fully, start the sweep, and keep your wrist raised with Spectra active until it finishes. The first Start after launching Spectra shows a setup reminder: **Start Sweep** continues; **Not Now** starts nothing. Acknowledging it does not verify or change your setting. **Always On** can leave Spectra visible while inactive; visibility alone does not keep Bluetooth collection running. **Return to Clock** is a different setting. Spectra cannot change these system settings or guarantee active time on every Watch.
sections.title: Keep the display fully awake

sections.body: If Spectra becomes inactive or you leave it during collection, the sweep ends and preserves the evidence already retained as partial. It does not resume when you return. An early stop, Bluetooth loss, or a retention limit can also reduce coverage. Review the reason, adjust your setup, and start a new sweep when ready. A timer finishing does not prove every nearby device was observed.
sections.title: An interruption keeps a partial capture

sections.body: Open Spectra on your paired iPhone once to prepare transfer. After each new sweep, the Watch saves the capture before automatically queuing it for your paired iPhone. **Queued** means delivery is pending; **Received on iPhone** confirms local storage, not completed recognition. Open Spectra on iPhone to identify received signals and add them to **Sessions** automatically. No need to keep the Watch completion screen open. Choose **New Sweep** to collect again, or open **Saved sweeps** from the tray button to review transfer status and retry when needed. Transfers may wait for connectivity or Apple’s scheduling. **Settings** → **Experimental Watch** on iPhone provides processing and transfer help. Older captures sent before automatic handoff may still offer **Add to Sessions**.
sections.title: Finish on Watch, review on iPhone

sections.body: Look for the Watch-with-radio-waves icon and **Apple Watch · Bluetooth-only sweep** label. They identify where the evidence was collected, not a search for nearby watches. Your custom name never replaces this origin label, and rechecks keep it along with the original capture time. **Experimental** and partial-capture status stay visible. Blue icons identify original captures; violet icons and a **Recheck** number identify later interpretations. Review **Coverage**: even a complete 30-second capture cannot confirm that every nearby device was observed.
sections.title: Find your Watch sweep in Sessions

sections.body: Each device retains up to five capture copies, bounded to 4 MiB each. When space is needed, the Watch retires only copies confirmed received on iPhone; the phone retires only inbox copies already processed into **Sessions**. Unsent or unprocessed evidence is not automatically discarded. Saved **Sessions** are not automatically removed to make room. If session history is full, remove sessions you no longer need and retry phone processing; the unprocessed inbox copy remains. A full capture store with no eligible copies stops accepting new captures; review transfer or processing status before retrying. If capture storage cannot load, use **Retry Loading** before choosing erasure. It rechecks local storage without erasing copies; transfer or processing failures have their own retry actions. Watch sweeps save to **Sessions** independently of the **Save completed sessions** setting for iPhone checks.
sections.title: Room for the next sweep

sections.body: **Reset Spectra** on iPhone erases its sessions, received Watch data, and preferences, then requests erasure of captures, diagnostics, and preferences in the known paired Watch app. **Watch reset pending** means the Watch has not confirmed erasure; an offline Watch may still hold data. Keep the devices paired and open Spectra on Watch to finish. **Watch reset confirmed** appears only after the Watch reports completion. When the Watch receives a reset, it stops collection and discards any unfinished sweep. System permissions and files exported or shared elsewhere remain.
sections.title: Confirm a reset on both devices

sections.body: In Spectra on iPhone, open **Settings** and review the **Apple Watch** section. **Watch reset not ready** can mean the paired Watch app has not introduced itself or needs an update. Open or update Spectra on both devices, then explicitly choose **Reset Watch** and confirm. A newly paired or reinstalled Watch is not automatically erased by an earlier request. If **Watch reset needs attention** appears, follow the recovery guidance; do not assume erasure succeeded. No paired Watch means there is no Watch reset to request.
sections.title: If the Watch reset is not ready

sections.body: Captures can contain advertised names, manufacturer and service bytes, signal strength, timestamps, and session-scoped identity tokens. These fields can identify devices or people. Spectra uses protected local storage marked for exclusion from backups and Apple’s paired-device transfer; it does not upload captures to Arc Signal or an identification service. Operating-system backup behavior remains under Apple’s control.
sections.title: Captured on Watch, reviewed on iPhone

steps: Install the Watch companion and open Spectra on iPhone once. Set the Watch’s **Wake Duration** to 70 seconds.
Tap to wake the Watch fully, start a sweep, and keep Spectra active for the 30-second window.
Review completion or interruption status. New captures are saved and queued for your paired iPhone automatically.

Open Spectra on iPhone and review **Sessions** once processing finishes. Review findings and **Coverage** before drawing conclusions; use **Settings** → **Experimental Watch** if a transfer needs attention.
content.takeaway: Capture without your iPhone nearby. Save up to five Bluetooth sweeps on your Watch, then review findings on your paired iPhone. This companion is experimental—not a background scanner.

technicalSections.body: The Watch retains bounded advertisement evidence, not every radio packet. Callback timing is delivery timing, not proof of uninterrupted sampling. Repeated callbacks do not establish separate physical devices; a product can change identifiers. Names and protocol fields are unauthenticated claims. Recognition on iPhone cannot recover information the Watch did not retain. Recorded signal strength was measured by the Watch, not the iPhone; readings taken later with the phone can differ.
technicalSections.title: Observation is bounded

technicalSections.body: For an eligible saved Watch finding, **Bluetooth Proximity** searches for possible matching broadcasts near your iPhone and asks you to confirm a candidate. It cannot reuse a Watch identity as a verified iPhone target or turn recorded Watch strength into a live reading. Matching names or payloads can come from different devices. The new signal measurement is taken by the iPhone; it does not verify identity or measure distance from the Watch.
technicalSections.title: A new proximity check uses the iPhone

technicalSections.body: Watch captures, the iPhone inbox, imported **Sessions**, and timing diagnostics are separate stores. **Erase Inbox Copies** leaves imported sessions intact. Individual session deletion leaves inbox and Watch copies intact. **Erase All Sessions** also clears the received Watch inbox, but does not request a Watch reset. Watch copies remain after those actions. **Reset Spectra** additionally clears received diagnostics and preferences and requests a paired Watch reset. Previously queued copies cannot silently restore erased iPhone data. Erasing captures directly on Watch cancels queued transfers where possible, but already delivered or in-flight phone copies may remain. Exported files and system permissions are not erased.
technicalSections.title: Copies have separate erase controls

technicalSections.body: A protected local reset-status record survives a reset so Spectra can finish an offline Watch request and reject stale commands or transfers. It contains random coordination identifiers and request status, not captured signals. A reset request applies only to the Watch app installation it names. Repeated delivery of an already completed request does not erase a new sweep. Confirmation describes completion of that request, not a promise that the Watch can never collect new data.
technicalSections.title: Why a small reset record remains

technicalSections.body: Watch diagnostics are separate from scan captures. They retain up to 20 recent timing and count reports per device, including Watch model, OS/build, completion status and lifecycle events, but no nearby-device names, identity values or advertisement payloads. Use **Share Watch diagnostics** on iPhone to deliberately share received reports for troubleshooting. Dates and hardware details can still reveal context. Nothing is sent to support automatically.
technicalSections.title: Share timing diagnostics only when needed

content.title: Try the Experimental Watch collector

content.important: A strong signal is not proof of a hidden or recording device. It does not necessarily belong to the closest device.

sections.body: **Strong**, **Moderate**, and **Faint** describe the signal received by your iPhone. Walls, bodies, reflections, antenna orientation, and transmit power can change the reading—even when neither device moves.
sections.title: Read the band, not a distance

sections.body: A device found only through your joined Wi-Fi network has no measurable physical proximity in Spectra. Its network presence cannot tell you which room it is in.
sections.title: Network presence is different

sections.body: **Briefly observed** means only one or two usable Bluetooth signal readings were retained. **Repeatedly observed** means at least three were retained. These labels describe observation, not an authenticated device model or continuous presence. A weak or intermittent advertiser may produce only a brief sighting.
sections.title: Briefly or repeatedly observed

sections.body: **Bluetooth Proximity** starts a fresh, unsaved listen; it never reuses an old reading as a live measurement. New Bluetooth captures saved on this iPhone can retain a private reference so their framework identities can be recognized after reopening, including from a recheck. A changed identity or silent device may still be unavailable. Older sessions, imported files, and Watch captures may offer possible matches based on a broadcast name, a separately labeled **System name**, or supported payload evidence. Confirm a suggestion before following it; similar names or bytes do not prove it is the same physical device.
sections.title: Follow a signal from a saved check

sections.body: Use **Quick Check** or **Area Sweep** with Bluetooth selected, or **Monitor** while stationary. Recognizable names for AirTag, Tile, Chipolo, Pebblebee, Galaxy SmartTag, and eufy SmartTrack can appear as Possible item-tracker matches. **Finding-network accessory** and **Finding-network broadcast** describe recognized formats, not a specific tracker; phones, computers and headphones may also participate. Open a finding for its evidence or select it for **Bluetooth Proximity**. These results describe nearby signal presence, not ownership or movement with you. Trackers may change identifiers or omit recognizable names, so Spectra cannot identify every tracker or rule one out when no match appears.
sections.title: Recognize nearby item trackers

steps: Choose **Check Bluetooth Proximity** in results, then select a found device. Its individual details can open it directly.
**Start Signal Check** to see live dBm readings. A saved result may require confirming a possible match; a name does not verify identity.
Mark a stable reference, move a little, then pause in a similar phone orientation. Compare the live reading and the change in dB from your reference.
content.takeaway: Use signal strength to compare observations—not to measure distance.

technicalSections.body: The live number shows received signal strength (RSSI) in dBm. Less-negative values are stronger: −40 dBm is stronger than −80 dBm. After ten seconds without a reading, the current value is replaced by **No current reading**; the previous value remains time-labeled briefly. Silence does not mean zero signal or prove a device has left. The reference comparison uses the median of up to six recent readings and shows the change in dB, not metres or a bearing. **Technical details** retain the earlier check’s signal evidence.
technicalSections.title: The underlying measurement

technicalSections.body: A similarity set shows the range across its currently observed Bluetooth identities rather than averaging unlike signals. Expand it to inspect each identity and its own measurement. A physical device may advertise more than one identity.
technicalSections.title: Several identities in one result

technicalSections.body: iOS 27 Channel Sounding requires a paired, connected accessory with compatible hardware. It cannot range arbitrary broadcasts. Spectra keeps discovery connection-free and compares received signal strength instead; it does not display invented meters or direction.
technicalSections.title: Why not precise Bluetooth ranging?

technicalSections.body: A complete Google Find Hub frame can support **Finding-network accessory**. The Apple offline-finding layout documented in published research can support **Finding-network broadcast**. These unauthenticated formats do not establish a manufacturer, model, lost-device state or reporting activity; programmable devices can imitate them. Spectra does not decode their identifiers, query an account, or connect to identify an AirTag. Raw fields and sources remain available in technical details.
technicalSections.title: What finding-network labels mean

content.title: What Bluetooth signal means

content.important: A shared name, vendor, or signal strength does not establish one physical device. Bluetooth and network identities are not merged across radios.

sections.body: Several local-network services may appear together when their advertised relationship suggests the same endpoint. Expand the group to see its services and why they were linked.
sections.title: Likely network endpoints

sections.body: Signals with similar broadcasts can share a similarity set. Its members may be separate devices; Spectra keeps their individual records. **Observed pattern** describes the strongest relevant member’s evidence tier, not identity confidence or proof that the signals belong together. The separate match badge and amber **Similarity only** caution still apply. Signal and service-signal counts describe retained records, not physical-device totals.
sections.title: Similar is not the same

sections.body: **Summary** puts named findings and related signal profiles in one list, even when a match is only **Possible** or its device type is unknown. Each card shows its confidence and whether it represents one identity, likely related network services, or similar broadcasts that may be separate devices. Higher-evidence findings come first; items you marked expected stay at the end. **Monitor** distinguishes **Since baseline**, **Starting baseline**, and **Earlier observations** retained from before the current comparison. These sections describe observation time, not trusted or untrusted devices. The same names and device-type icons appear in analysis and proximity choices. A manufacturer code alone is not a device name. Unnamed, low-evidence activity stays expandable; **All Signals** retains every source identity and area clue. Visibility does not increase confidence or mark a finding as dangerous.
sections.title: One list, with context on each result

sections.body: Device icons describe a **possible hardware category**, not activity. A reviewed MacBook match can use a laptop; an uncertain subtype uses its supported parent category. Known electronic identities without a suitable specific icon use a **chip**. Conflicting product claims never borrow one model's icon. The **confidence badge** and source evidence remain separate: a more specific icon does not make a match stronger. A type already stated in reviewed text need not repeat; its **Possible** qualifier and source context still apply. A known product can still have no reviewed capability evidence. Names and icons do not verify a manufacturer, owner, recording or playback.
sections.title: Hardware icons, separate confidence

sections.body: An otherwise unclassified radio finding uses a neutral source icon: **radio waves** for Bluetooth, a **network** for local-network observations, or a **dotted circle** for mixed or unavailable radio-source information. The icon does not identify hardware or imply Wi-Fi-wide scanning. Supported hardware or capability icons stay **blue**, including in similarity sets. The amber **Similarity only** caution still means the identities may be separate devices; blue does not make their relationship or identity certain.
sections.title: Unknown type, observed source

sections.body: Use **Filters** to narrow results by the measurement that recorded them: **Bluetooth**, **Local network**, or **Magnetic**. Choose any combination and **Apply**; leave all unchecked to include everything. The button is hidden when only one measurement is represented. **Search names** looks for the displayed or broadcast name, including names whose device type is undetermined. It does not guess categories from your search. **Cancel** keeps the current measurement filter; **Clear filters** restores all results and clears name search. Device-type labels are helpful estimates, not exclusion rules. **Filters** and search never change collection, saved reports, or export scope.
sections.title: Filter what was found

steps: Expand a **Summary** result to inspect its members and grouping explanation. Large groups offer **Show all** with their signal count: a searchable list of that group’s individual records, also available in specialist checks. Choose a signal to open its details. Matching results appear before related context; this list never merges similar signals into one device.

Choose **All Signals** above **Results** for the exact retained inventory, or **Show signals** to expand unclassified activity. If **Summary** and **All Signals** look alike, the check may contain only separate identities without supported relationships.
content.takeaway: Fewer cards make results easier to explore. They are not a count of confirmed physical devices.

technicalSections.body: Repeated callbacks for the same exact framework identity accumulate in one record during a check. A rotating Bluetooth identifier can still create another record; the app does not assume it is the same physical device.
technicalSections.title: Repeated observations

technicalSections.body: Bonjour grouping uses a session-scoped hint based on service instance, domain, and interface. It is evidence of a likely endpoint relationship, not authenticated hardware identity. Every service retains its exact record.
technicalSections.title: The local-network relationship

technicalSections.body: Ordinary new checks use fresh session identifiers and do not automatically link devices across history. An explicit **Bluetooth Proximity** check can reuse a retained private reference for the selected iPhone capture; it does not merge sessions or authenticate hardware. Similarity sets and compact disclosures change presentation, not the underlying retained evidence.
technicalSections.title: A new check starts fresh

content.title: How signals are grouped

content.important: Speakers, magnets, metal, wiring, chargers, and phone cases can all change the field. A spike cannot identify a device or show its distance or intent. No change does not rule out a device.

sections.body: The magnetometer measures at one small sensor—not across the whole phone. Its location varies by iPhone model. Move slowly over the same spot, keeping the phone’s angle and gap consistent.
sections.title: Where to aim your iPhone

sections.body: On iPhone 17 Pro Max, use the lower back near the USB-C end, not the camera area. Apple’s dimensional drawing marks the compass in this lower-back area. This is a model-specific location, not a universal iPhone scanning point. The camera and contactless-payment area are not a reliable guide to magnetometer placement.
sections.title: Example: iPhone 17 Pro Max

sections.body: Try a practice sweep with an ordinary speaker you own before exploring an unfamiliar space. Keep a gap; do not press magnets against the phone. No change does not rule out a device. In the app, choose **Practice with the magnetometer** here or before beginning a magnetic **Area Sweep**, then tap **Start Practice**. Compare a familiar speaker with a spot away from electronics, repeat the same slow pass, and watch **Actual Field** and **Δ Reference**. Learn which phone positions produce a repeatable response without expecting a particular number. This is familiarization, not calibration or a pass/fail test of the phone. Practice uses live magnetic readings and motion context only: no Bluetooth, local-network discovery, device findings, exports, or saved session. **Stop Practice**, **Done**, or leaving the app clears the practice readings. Returning does not resume measurement; tap **Start Practice** to try again. Begin a separate **Area Sweep** with a fresh reference before reviewing a space.
sections.title: Practice before an unfamiliar-space sweep

sections.body: Some devices produce little detectable magnetic change. Sensor position, distance, shielding, and magnetic accessories can also affect the response. No change does not rule out a device. A speaker’s magnet may cause a local change, but not every speaker or microphone produces a change the phone can resolve at your position. Watch **Actual Field** or **Δ Reference**, not just the saved event count. Confirm that live readings are arriving in **Measurement Details**; an unavailable or stale reading is not a quiet field.
sections.title: Near a device, but no change?

sections.body: Pause away from obvious magnets or electronics so a stable display reference can form. Use **Rebuild Reference** to choose a fresh display comparison point. Automatic event detection has its own calibrated baseline.
sections.title: Establish a comparison point

sections.body: If prompted, make one gentle figure eight and then pause. If calibration stays limited, the actual-field trace can continue even though automatic spike marking is unavailable.
sections.title: Follow the calibration guidance

sections.body: Automatic detection has its own baseline and adaptive threshold. A sustained change or an unusually strong spike can create an event. Ordinary small fluctuations should not.
sections.title: A fluctuation is not always an event

sections.body: Saved magnetic graph retains a downsampled, bounded view of display readings, independently of detector events. Choose **Review graph** in completed or saved results, switch **Actual field** or **Δ Reference**, and move the slider to inspect a reading. Reference changes and missing readings break the line. Older checks without graph data cannot recreate it.
sections.title: Review the graph after finishing

steps: Choose **Motion and magnetic** for an **Area Sweep**. Remove magnetic cases, mounts, or attached accessories if practical, then establish a reference away from obvious magnetic sources.

To get familiar with the response, use an ordinary speaker you own. Without touching it, slowly pass different parts of the phone over the same spot, holding the angle and gap steady. Repeat the path; do not press a strong magnet against the phone or open equipment. A flat response is inconclusive, not proof the sensor failed.
Switch between **Actual Field** and **Δ Reference** to make changes easier to see.
Review the event timeline for meaningful spikes, then revisit the area to see whether the change repeats.
content.takeaway: **Actual Field** shows the measurement. **Δ Reference** shows how far it has moved from your display reference.

technicalSections.body: The display reference supports the actual/delta graph. The event detector independently evaluates calibrated samples against a noise-adaptive threshold with persistence and strong-spike rules. Rebuilding the display reference does not erase events or reset the detector.
technicalSections.title: Two different baselines

technicalSections.body: Events retain time, duration, measured field at the strongest change, signed change from the detector baseline, and threshold overage. These are magnetic excursions—not identified speakers, microphones, or other devices.
technicalSections.title: What an event records

technicalSections.body: **Measurement Details** exposes calibration, motion quality, and baseline status. Abrupt movement and unusable calibration remain excluded from event detection even while the actual-field trace is visible.
technicalSections.title: Measurement quality

technicalSections.body: Half-second buckets preserve actual-field and delta extrema plus endpoints. At most 2,048 points are retained; long sweeps keep the most recent graph window and show an earlier-points-omitted notice. This is not a continuous recording. The graph does not determine which changes qualify as detector events.
technicalSections.title: What the graph keeps

content.title: Reading the magnetic meter

content.important: Keep Spectra open. Locking the iPhone or switching apps ends measurement. Monitor is not an unattended or background security alarm.

sections.body: Monitor starts establishing a baseline automatically. Keep the iPhone stationary: each available radio source needs 30 seconds of active observation. Permission waiting does not count. The countdown follows the slowest participating source. **Observe 30 seconds longer** extends that comparison once to 60 seconds per source. When the baseline is ready, the change counters start at zero and the panel shows its capture time and elapsed comparison time. No duration guarantees discovery of every device.
sections.title: Give the starting comparison time

sections.body: Baseline signals remain in the final inventory. A potentially concerning device already present is not cleared or hidden. A device first observed during baseline collection becomes part of that starting comparison; one first observed afterward is newly observed, not necessarily newly arrived.
sections.title: Initially observed does not mean trusted

sections.body: The **Newly observed**, **Returned**, and **Not recently seen** rows count distinct signal identities in the current comparison’s latest 40 retained change events. Repeated changes for the same identity count once in each row. Counts may decrease as older events leave that bounded history. One identity can appear in more than one row, so do not add these counts as a total device count. **Mark changes reviewed** acknowledges the latest change without zeroing these counters, trusting a device, changing the baseline, or erasing evidence.
sections.title: Read changes at a glance

sections.body: Tap **New Baseline** in the main Monitor panel when you want a fresh reference, such as after moving the phone or changing networks. The tap starts a new 30-second observation window immediately; it does not simply clear the numbers. When the new baseline is ready, its change counters begin at zero. Earlier comparisons and their retained events remain in the same session for review after **Stop Monitor**. Wait for the current baseline to finish before starting another. Up to nine comparisons fit in one session; stop and start another **Monitor** when that limit is reached. Spectra does not automatically judge that you moved or silently replace your baseline.
sections.title: Choose a fresh comparison

steps: Choose **Monitor** and the radio measurements you need. Place the phone where it can stay.
Wait for the starting comparison, then glance at the change summary. Do not interpret a quiet screen as an all-clear.
Choose **Stop Monitor** to explore named/grouped results, repeat counts, change times, and any earlier comparisons.
content.takeaway: Keep the iPhone stationary and watch for observation changes—not a stream of device arrivals.

technicalSections.body: The **Not recently seen** label means that a previously observed identity has stopped being observed. For Bluetooth, Spectra waits 45 seconds without an observation before showing it. For local-network services, it follows Bonjour announcements and removals. Sleep, identity rotation, interference, and changing broadcast behavior can produce changes without physical movement. Matching names or vendors never justify combining separate identities.
technicalSections.title: Why did an identity disappear or return?

technicalSections.body: **Coverage** describes source loss rather than calling every device gone. A late or recovering source gets a 30-second source-local observation window; its initial identities join that source’s comparison instead of creating a burst of apparent arrivals. A network reconnection can change which services are visible; use a new baseline when the surroundings or network have changed.
technicalSections.title: What happens when a source stops?

technicalSections.body: Each comparison retains up to 40 recent raw change events. The display combines the same identity and change type, with retained occurrence count and first/latest times; full JSON preserves retained raw events. Counts may change as older events leave this bounded history. Radio intensity is not a measure of risk.
technicalSections.title: Bounded events, not a lifetime counter

content.title: Understand Monitor and its baseline

content.important: For a repeatable problem, contact support@arcsignal.zendesk.com or open **Support site** in Spectra **Settings**. Start with support information, the steps taken, and what you expected. Do not send private scan results unless you deliberately choose to share them.

sections.body: The device may be silent, sleeping, already connected without recognizable advertisements, on another network, or outside current recognition coverage. Some watches expose more information only in discovery or workout modes. Use general **Quick Check** or **Area Sweep** to include unclassified activity; specialist checks show only supported matches. Longer listening may help an intermittent signal but cannot reveal fields the device or iOS does not supply. Do not connect to unknown equipment to force a result.
sections.title: My known device does not appear

sections.body: An Apple, Garmin, Samsung, or other company code alone does not identify a wearable. Generic heart-rate services can also come from chest straps. Distinctive names can support a possible product match; selected historical protocol patterns remain explicitly uncertain and may not appear on current firmware. **Watches & Wearables** includes supported watches, fitness bands, smart rings, and other wearables. A silent device or a generic service can remain unclassified; use a general check to inspect that activity. A wearable match cannot tell whether a microphone is active.
sections.title: Why a nearby watch or ring can remain unknown

sections.body: A broadcast name is self-reported and can be renamed or copied. Company identifiers sometimes identify a chip or protocol namespace, not the retail manufacturer. **Possible** and **Probable** are evidence labels, not numeric probabilities. Conflicting product claims stay ambiguous; details explain the supporting evidence. Catalog updates ship with app updates; Spectra does not download identification data during a scan.
sections.title: The name or type looks wrong

sections.body: Some devices produce little detectable magnetic change. Sensor position, distance, shielding, and magnetic accessories can also affect the response. No change does not rule out a device. The sensor is a small point inside the phone, not its entire back. See **Reading the magnetic meter** for positioning and a safe comparison exercise. On iPhone 17 Pro Max, use the lower back near the USB-C end, not the camera area. Check that live readings are arriving before interpreting a flat graph.
sections.title: The magnetic reading barely changes near a device

sections.body: Actual field and display delta can work before the calibrated event detector is ready. A 0/25-style sample count describes accepted detector-baseline readings, not permission progress. Follow the current readiness instruction, pause away from obvious magnets, and check **Measurement Details**. Strong absolute field alone is not a qualifying relative excursion. Try removing a magnetic case or mount if practical.
sections.title: The graph moves but no spike is saved

sections.body: Internet access does not prove local discovery works. Guest isolation, blocked multicast, unadvertised service types, separate subnets, or a denied Local Network permission can prevent results. Check **Coverage** and the joined network. Spectra is not a scanner for all Wi-Fi radios and does not probe arbitrary ports.
sections.title: Wi-Fi works but no devices appear

sections.body: Keep Spectra visible. Locking, switching apps, permission changes, source loss, and ending early can limit a check. **Check ended early** marks a foreground interruption; returning does not resume the check. **Check interrupted** offers **Review Coverage** to inspect the problem and **Review Results** to finish reviewing available measurements, even if there are no signal findings. Confirm the separate saved status before closing. Restore access if needed, then start a fresh check from **Scan**. An incomplete check is not a no-match result. On a busy scan, wait until collection finishes to explore stable detailed results.
sections.title: A check stopped or looks incomplete

sections.body: **Some observations were not retained** does not by itself mean the result list or device storage is full. Read recorded reasons in **Coverage**. Repeated readings can be combined routinely; inventory and endpoint counts have different units. **Result retention limit reached** means some observations could not add a new result record at that limit. **Result records retired** means earlier records were removed from the bounded retained list. Retained results remain available; these notices alone do not require restarting or prove collection stopped. Older captures may not record a breakdown.
sections.title: Does an observation notice mean storage is full?

sections.body: Choose a supported **Technical archive**, not **Analysis JSON** or **Reduced identifying information**. A failed checksum or malformed file is different from an older archive with **Checksum unavailable**. Use the original exporter to create another technical archive when possible; a newer unsupported schema may require a Spectra update. If history is full, manage saved sessions before retrying; Spectra does not remove existing history for an import. If file or protected-storage access is unavailable, unlock the iPhone and retry the appropriate access step. Canceling file selection is not an import failure.
sections.title: A file cannot be imported

steps: Open **Coverage** and read the reason for each partial or unavailable measurement.
Check iPhone **Settings** if access was denied, return to Spectra, and repeat the smallest affected check.

In Spectra **Settings**, use **Copy support information**, then **Support site** or **Email support**. The copy includes version, build, iOS, hardware model, detection-engine revision and catalog revision—not scan data.
content.takeaway: First check coverage and measurement state. A missing observation is not evidence that nothing is there.

technicalSections.body: Live radios, sensors, and the screen use power. Finish checks you no longer need. Keep the phone ventilated and follow iOS temperature warnings; Spectra cannot guarantee identical performance across all hardware or conditions. In a dense environment, read the recorded observation-handling reason in **Coverage** rather than treating a count as proof that the result list is full.
technicalSections.title: Heat, battery, and dense environments

technicalSections.body: Include the scan mode, selected sources, approximate duration, permission state, whether the app was interrupted, and exact error text. Screenshots may include personal broadcast names; review them before sending. The support clipboard expires after ten minutes and is not shared through Universal Clipboard. **Support site** opens arcsignal.zendesk.com; **Email support** opens your mail app. Zendesk handles information you submit. Nothing is attached or sent automatically. For company and product information, **Arc Signal website** in **Settings** → **About** opens arcsignal.app. For Watch help, start from Spectra **Settings** on your paired iPhone and include the Watch version and build from its **About** screen.
technicalSections.title: Help us reproduce it safely

content.title: Troubleshoot unexpected results

content.important: Advertised device names can contain personal information. Those names may appear in results and saved checks on this iPhone.

sections.body: Spectra processes observations and Apple Intelligence explanations on device. It does not automatically share your results or capture camera frames or microphone recordings. External sharing is a separate choice.
sections.title: On-device processing, optional sharing

sections.body: New captures save the collector platform, hardware model, OS version, and app version and build locally. This helps distinguish Watch and iPhone evidence without using personal device names, serial numbers, or persistent device identifiers. Rechecks preserve the original collection context rather than replacing it with the current phone’s information. Exporting or sharing can disclose this context.
sections.title: Collection context stays with the report

sections.body: Set up access in Spectra’s **Settings** tab or when you start a check. Spectra checks selected sources again before scanning and explains when a source cannot run. Setup does not create a saved session. The camera and microphone are not accessed.
sections.title: You choose what gets measured

sections.body: Completed checks are saved locally by default. Turning saving off keeps future checks out of history; it does not delete reports you already saved or prevent a deliberate **Import Session** or recheck. Saved sessions are not automatically removed to make room. Individual deletion offers a brief **Undo** using one temporary in-memory copy after removing the saved copy. Leaving **Sessions** or switching away from Spectra ends Undo; bulk erasure and reset also clear it. No Recently Deleted folder is kept. The Sessions guide explains the time window and separate copies.
sections.title: History is your choice

sections.body: **Import Session** reads a supported **Technical archive** locally and asks you to review it before saving. **Imported** identifies a restored record, not a fresh measurement or authenticated capture. Recorded names, notes, collector details, and any location remain claims from the file. Import does not start scanning, analysis, or a map, and does not alter the source file. Private Bluetooth follow-up references are never restored from JSON. Review sensitive contents before choosing to import or share them.
sections.title: Restore a file deliberately

sections.body: The Experimental Watch collector saves bounded Bluetooth evidence locally, including names and payloads that may identify people or devices. New sweeps automatically transfer to your paired iPhone and are identified and added to **Sessions** when Spectra is active, even if automatic iPhone scan saving is off. There is no cloud upload. Each device keeps up to five recent capture copies; only safely received Watch copies or processed phone inbox copies can make room automatically. Watch copies, the phone inbox, **Sessions**, and timing diagnostics have separate erase controls. **Reset Spectra** on iPhone clears received Watch data, rejects previously queued deliveries, and requests a reset of the known paired Watch app. An offline Watch may still hold data until it confirms erasure. The Experimental Watch guide explains pending resets, storage limits, and deletion. Exported or shared files remain.
sections.title: Experimental Watch has separate copies

sections.body: Open **Privacy policy** from **Welcome** or Spectra **Settings** → **About** for the public policy, including local observations, permissions, erasure, optional exports, support correspondence, and website hosting. Reading the website requires an internet connection; this practical Guide stays available offline.
sections.title: Read the full privacy policy

sections.body: **Export JSON** on completed or saved results lets you choose **Analysis JSON**, **Technical archive**, or **Reduced identifying information**. **Analysis JSON** includes meaningful retained evidence and your notes; the technical archive also includes raw retained data and saved graphs. All formats exclude generated AI explanations. Reduced omits identifying text and raw payloads but is not anonymous. All formats ignore visible results filters. Nothing is uploaded automatically.
sections.title: Share only when you choose

sections.body: Selecting one finding in **Copy for AI analysis** prepares its data and a prompt locally. Review the preview and privacy notice; only tapping **Copy prompt and finding** writes to the clipboard. Names and optional technical data may identify devices or people; the default copy is not anonymous either. Spectra requests an on-device-only clipboard item that expires after ten minutes. Pasting into another app shares it under its policies; expiration or **Reset Spectra** cannot recall copies already shared. No AI app opens and nothing uploads automatically.
sections.title: Copying a finding for another AI app

steps: Use **Save completed sessions** in Spectra **Settings** to control future history saving.
Open **Sessions** to delete one report, use **Select** for several, or **Erase All Sessions** to also remove recovery copies and received Watch inbox captures. Watch copies remain.

Use **Reset Spectra** in Spectra **Settings** to erase local sessions and preferences, return to **Welcome**, and request a paired Watch reset. Check the Watch reset status separately; a pending request is not confirmed erasure. System permissions and copies you saved or shared elsewhere remain.
content.takeaway: No account. No advertising or analytics SDK. Observations stay on your devices unless you choose to share them.

technicalSections.body: Saved reports and notes use iOS file protection. New on-device AI explanations are temporary: they are not saved in sessions or included in exports. Older sessions may still contain explanations saved by an earlier app version; deleting those sessions removes that local history too. Spectra marks the session directory, including recovery copies, for exclusion from device backups. This is not a guarantee that sessions can never appear in a backup or on a restored device; iOS controls backup and restore behavior. Files you export may be stored or backed up by your chosen destination. The primary history file keeps up to **500 sessions** within **256 MiB**; originals, rechecks, and imported copies count toward these independent limits. Saved sessions are not automatically removed. Protected recovery copies also remain until deliberate erasure; **Erase All Sessions** and **Reset Spectra** include them. Newer local history formats may not open in older app builds. Return to a compatible build rather than erasing history you still need to resolve a version mismatch. Safe file replacement, protected recovery copies, and separate Watch inbox data can require additional disk space. The displayed history usage is not total app storage or an export file’s size. These are not tamper-evident forensic records or an unlimited archive.
technicalSections.title: Protected, bounded history

technicalSections.body: Each new capture uses its own identifiers. A saved iPhone Bluetooth capture can also retain a small, capture-specific reference in protected local history for an explicit **Bluetooth Proximity** check. It contains no raw Bluetooth framework identifier and is never included in JSON, AI copies, or Watch transfers. Its private index is marked for exclusion from device backups, subject to iOS backup behavior. Rechecks of that capture share its reference. Removing the last non-imported original or recheck copy retires its active local reference; imported copies cannot keep it. **Undo** can briefly restore it with the session. **Erase All Sessions** and **Reset Spectra** also clear protected recovery copies. Names remain unverified and may identify people or devices; resetting an identifier does not anonymize a transmitted name.
technicalSections.title: Session identifiers and saved signal checks

technicalSections.body: When selected, Spectra browses a fixed catalog of Bonjour services on the joined network. It does not pair with discovered devices or open application sessions to their endpoints.
technicalSections.title: What local-network access does

technicalSections.body: **Show Wi-Fi name** asks for location access set to **While Using the App**, with **Precise Location** enabled, because iOS requires it for this information. This Wi-Fi-name action does not request coordinates or save your network name; the name is cleared when the app backgrounds. Sensor scanning does not need Location access. The separate **Tag location** option requests a scan-start position only when you choose it. A network name does not identify your router or establish that it is safe.
technicalSections.title: The optional Wi-Fi name

technicalSections.body: **Tag location** is off for each new iPhone check. Turn it on before starting to request one nearby-in-time position, not a route or background tracking. A saved tag includes coordinates, estimated accuracy, and the fix time. It describes the collecting iPhone, not a detected device, room, or verified venue. No address lookup runs. The first tagged result offers **Enable map previews** or **Not now**. Enabling allows Apple Maps to load saved areas automatically when you view tagged results; declining is remembered without repeated prompts. Change **Automatic map previews** under **Settings** → **Session maps** at any time. **Open in Maps** separately shares the saved coordinates to explore there. Neither feature requests your current location through Spectra. Apple handles map requests under its own data practices. Spectra keeps the preview only temporarily, not in your session or exports. **Reset Spectra** clears the map preference; deleting sessions does not. Watch captures remain untagged.
technicalSections.title: An optional place in your own history

technicalSections.body: Every JSON format omits the tag by default, including **Technical archive**. **Include scan location** explicitly adds coordinates, accuracy, and the location timestamp—even to **Reduced identifying information**. This can reveal where you were. On-device finding summaries and **Copy for AI analysis** always omit the tag. **Remove location** changes only this session copy; other rechecks, protected recovery copies, or files already shared may still retain it. **Erase All Sessions** or **Reset Spectra** clears local session and recovery history, not external copies.
technicalSections.title: Location has its own sharing choice

content.title: Privacy and storage

content.important: Powered-off, silent, wired, shielded, cellular-only, or locally recording devices may not appear. No result guarantees that a space is clear.

sections.body: Bluetooth sees devices currently advertising in a form available to the app. Local Network sees supported services on your joined network—not all nearby Wi-Fi radios.
sections.title: Wireless visibility is limited

sections.body: Local Network browsing can send queries visible to other network participants. Guest isolation, blocked multicast, or a separate network can hide devices. Do not join an unfamiliar network merely to improve a scan.
sections.title: Network discovery is not covert

sections.body: Metal, magnets, wiring, and ordinary electronics can cause excursions. A quiet magnetic trace cannot rule out a microphone, camera, or other device.
sections.title: Magnetic changes are not identities

steps: Review **Coverage** to distinguish a source you did not select from one that was unavailable or only partially observed.
Compare repeatable observations and inspect the surroundings. Treat device names, reflections, and magnetic spikes as clues to investigate.
content.takeaway: A completed check tells you what Spectra observed—not everything that might be present.

technicalSections.body: Keep Spectra visible during measurement. A foreground interruption ends an active scan with a coverage limitation and **Check ended early** status; returning does not resume collection. Review retained results and **Coverage** before starting another check. Monitor is not an unrestricted background detector.
technicalSections.title: Foreground operation

technicalSections.body: Live observation buffers and the retained result list have separate limits. Repeated readings may be combined before processing; other observations may be omitted at a buffer or retention boundary, or during shutdown. **Coverage** distinguishes recorded reasons and retired result records; older captures may record a total without its source or reason. These counts do not measure missing devices, free disk space, or whether collection stopped. **All Signals** means every retained record, not every transmission in the environment.
technicalSections.title: Busy-environment limits

content.title: Capabilities and blind spots

content.important: Deleting or resetting Spectra cannot delete exports, email attachments, or files already saved elsewhere. iOS permissions also remain under **Settings** control.

sections.body: **Sessions** groups checks by their original capture day, newest first, with the newest capture times first inside each day. The most recent day starts open; tap any date heading to show or hide its sessions. Each heading counts all saved versions for that day, including rechecks. You can keep several days open, and your choices stay in place while moving between tabs or opening and returning from a session. These choices are not saved across app launches. A new most-recent day starts open; deleting all history or changing time zone can reset the day groups. Each row keeps its check-type or Watch-origin icon even after you rename it.
sections.title: Find a check by day

sections.body: A Watch-with-radio-waves icon and **Apple Watch · Bluetooth-only sweep** label identify a session collected by the Experimental Watch companion. This is a general Bluetooth sweep from your Watch—not the **Watches & Wearables** specialist check on iPhone. The origin label stays visible after renaming and on rechecks. **Experimental** and any partial-capture status remain visible too. Original icons are blue; rechecks are violet and also say **Recheck**. Open **Coverage** to see collection limits before drawing conclusions.
sections.title: Recognize a sweep collected on Watch

sections.body: Each row shows its name, scan type, original capture time and duration, collector, recorded measurement scope, and a results summary. The small icon beside the scan type is a visual cue; the text identifies the check. **Partial coverage** or **Some measurements unavailable** means the listed measurements did not all complete. Older sessions may show **Source not recorded**, **Measurements not recorded**, or **Source and measurements not recorded**. Spectra does not guess. If the list says **Collection details in saved results**, open the session to review its original metadata. Watch rows retain **Experimental** and any early or interrupted completion status.
sections.title: Read a session at a glance

sections.body: **Estimated size** appears below each row’s capture time to help you compare larger saved sessions before deleting. It includes recorded capture data and that session’s saved list information, such as its name and notes. **KiB** and **MiB** use binary units. Shared history information, protected recovery copies, received Watch captures and exports are separate, so row estimates do not add up to the history total and deletion may free a different amount. A recheck or imported copy has its own size. An unavailable estimate is not shown; it does not mean the session is empty.
