sections.title: Compare saved sizes

sections.body: Tap the recheck count beneath an original session to show its saved interpretations, newest recheck first. Original icons are blue; recheck icons are violet and include a **Recheck** number. Renaming does not separate related copies. Each version opens, exports, and deletes independently. If the original was removed, the latest surviving recheck stays visible and says **Original removed**; any earlier rechecks remain expandable. Rechecks retain the original capture time and duration beside the scan type and show a separate evaluation date and time.
sections.title: Keep rechecks with their capture

sections.body: Saving completed sessions is on by default and can be changed in Spectra **Settings**. Turning it off affects future saving, not existing history or a deliberate import or recheck. The completed check tells you whether it was saved. If saving fails, keep the results open to review, use **Export JSON**, or **Retry Saving** when offered. For a history limit, **Manage Sessions** lets you remove copies you no longer need before retrying. Managing history does not save or discard the open result. A forced close, crash, or shutdown before saving can lose it; there is no continuous autosaved draft. Confirm important checks were saved before closing.
sections.title: Confirm a check was saved

sections.body: Choose **Import Session** in **Sessions** and select a file in Files, or open a compatible file with Spectra. Review the original capture time, recorded collector, compatibility, and integrity status, then choose **Import Session** to save it. **Cancel** leaves history unchanged. Only supported **Technical archive** files can restore a session; **Analysis JSON** and **Reduced identifying information** cannot. Files providers may need a connection to supply your chosen file; validation and saving run on device. Importing keeps the recorded acquisition and interpretation rather than collecting new evidence. **Imported** remains separate from the original collector and capture date. Opening a file while a check or another task is in progress waits for a safe point to review it; it does not discard the open results.
sections.title: Import a saved Technical archive

sections.body: New technical archives include a checksum. A matching checksum checks the archived bytes, not the author, collector, device identity, or truth of the measurements. Supported older archives can say **Checksum unavailable**; this is different from a failed integrity check. A failed checksum, malformed archive, or unsupported format cannot be imported. Importing does not start analysis, scanning, a recheck, or a map, and does not change the source file. Private Bluetooth follow-up references are not included in archives, so a later proximity check may require confirming a possible match.
sections.title: A checksum is not authentication

sections.body: Open a session and choose **Session options** → **Rename**, or use its list-row menu. Names can be up to 80 characters. Clearing a custom name restores the check-type name. Notes hold up to 1,000 characters of your own context; they do not become detector evidence. A rename does not change the original scan time.
sections.title: Give a session a useful name

sections.body: If you enabled **Tag location** and a usable fix arrived, **Scan start location** shows the iPhone’s recorded coordinates and estimated accuracy. On your first tagged result, choose **Enable map previews** to show saved areas automatically through Apple Maps, or **Not now** to keep coordinates only. Your choice is remembered. Change **Automatic map previews** under **Settings** → **Session maps** whenever you like. The marker describes the collecting iPhone; the shaded area represents its estimated accuracy, not where detected devices are. The preview does not request your current location or confirm a venue or room. **Open in Maps** is a separate choice for exploring the saved position in Maps. Maps opens only when you choose; previews load automatically only after you enable them. Rechecks inherit the selected copy’s original capture location, never your current position. A session without a tag cannot be assigned today’s location as though it were captured there. Watch sweeps remain untagged.
sections.title: Review or remove a saved location

sections.body: Saved coordinates and findings remain available if the optional preview fails or a connection is unavailable. Choose **Retry map preview** when offered, or **Open in Maps** to use Maps. Some regions near the poles cannot be represented by this preview; retry is not offered for an unsupported location. Spectra clears its temporary preview when you leave the results or switch away from the app; when you return, it can load again if **Automatic map previews** remains enabled. A failed preview does not continuously retry. Map requests are handled under Apple’s data practices. Clearing Spectra’s preview does not erase information or caches held by Apple Maps.
sections.title: When a map cannot load

sections.body: Choose **Session options** → **Remove location** and confirm to remove the tag from this copy without deleting its findings. Other sessions, rechecks, and exported files stay unchanged; remove their tags separately if needed. Protected recovery history can still contain an earlier copy. Use **Erase All Sessions** or **Reset Spectra** to clear local session and recovery history. Neither action recalls files already shared.
sections.title: A tag belongs to each saved copy

sections.body: A blue dot beside a session means newer recognition is available. Open it and choose **Recheck session**. A dot beside a collapsed recheck count means an eligible copy is inside; expand it to find that session. Spectra reinterprets compatible saved radio evidence using the engine and catalog bundled with your app update. It does not start Bluetooth or network discovery, collect new measurements, or upload your capture. Opening a session alone does not clear the dot.
sections.title: What does the blue dot mean?

sections.body: Yes. A recheck uses saved evidence, so you do not need to return to the location, join its network, or enable Apple Intelligence. Newer recognition may explain a previously unclear signal, but better matches are not guaranteed. Rechecking cannot recover measurements that were never retained or tell you what is at that location now. Run a new check there for a new observation.
sections.title: Can I recheck after leaving the location?

sections.body: A successful recheck saves a separate session named from the original naming base plus **Recheck 1**, **Recheck 2**, and so on. Rechecking a recheck does not stack suffixes. Each saved copy can be renamed independently, but its original naming base remains in recheck lineage and technical exports. **Rename** is not an erase action. The new result separates newly identified records, changed identifications, and previous matches no longer supported. These are interpretation changes—not newly discovered devices. **No identification changes** is also a valid outcome. **Captured** shows the original measurement date; **Rechecked** shows when the new interpretation was created.
sections.title: Your original stays unchanged

sections.body: Once a current recheck is saved, the blue dot clears for that capture family; earlier copies link to the latest interpretation. A later app update can make the newest usable copy eligible again. Deleting the current interpretation can restore eligibility on a surviving older copy. A missing revision or insufficient retained evidence can prevent rechecking; **Scan breakdown** explains why. Some older network records lack the original discovery fields. Unsupported records and saved magnetic readings are preserved, not reconstructed or treated as fresh measurements.
sections.title: When is another recheck useful?

sections.body: A recheck keeps its own retained evidence, so it uses additional local storage and counts toward the session limit. It never removes an existing session to make room. Requesting a recheck explicitly saves a new copy even if automatic saving of completed scans is off. Deleting the original does not delete its independent rechecks. If saving fails, follow the recovery advice shown, then retry. **Cancel** or leave the screen to stop pending work; a copy already saved at the moment you cancel remains in **Sessions**. **Erase All Sessions** and **Reset Spectra** include rechecks.
sections.title: Rechecks need room to save

sections.body: **Sessions** shows the saved count and primary history-file usage; **Settings** → **Privacy & storage** → **Session storage** provides storage details. History keeps up to **500 sessions** within **256 MiB**, with originals, rechecks, and imported copies counted separately. These limits are independent: free bytes do not provide another session slot, and an available slot does not guarantee a report will fit. Saving or importing never removes another session to make room. Export important copies, then delete those you no longer need before retrying. Exporting alone does not free history space. **On this iPhone** separately measures local capture files, including protected recovery, pending history files, and received Watch captures; it is not total app storage or free device space. Local history is marked for exclusion from backups; iOS controls backup and restore behavior. Export destinations have their own storage and backup policies.
sections.title: Make room without losing another session

sections.body: Swipe right on a session to reveal **Rename**, or swipe fully to open the name editor. Nothing changes until you save. Swipe left to reveal **Delete**, or swipe fully to delete that session. **Undo** briefly restores the most recently deleted session, including its name, notes, location tag, and retained evidence. It is available for 10 seconds, or 30 seconds when VoiceOver is running at deletion. Another deletion replaces the previous Undo opportunity. Leaving **Sessions**, switching away from Spectra, or starting confirmed bulk erasure or reset ends Undo. Spectra removes the saved copy first and keeps only one temporary in-memory recovery copy; there is no Recently Deleted folder.
sections.title: Swipe to rename or delete

sections.body: Use **Select** to delete several sessions with confirmation. Hiding a day or collapsing rechecks does not deselect hidden sessions: the date heading and recheck disclosure keep their selected counts, and **Delete Selected** shows the total. Expand the relevant group to change its selection. Deleting an original does not select or delete its rechecks. **Erase All Sessions** includes closed groups, recovery copies, and received Watch inbox captures; it is disabled when there is nothing to erase. Watch copies remain; this action does not request a Watch reset. Use **Settings** → **Experimental Watch** → **Erase Inbox Copies** to clear that inbox separately without deleting imported sessions. **Reset Spectra** additionally clears received Watch diagnostics and preferences, returns to **Welcome**, and requests a reset of the known paired Watch app. Check its separate pending or confirmed status. **Delete Selected**, **Erase All Sessions**, and **Reset Spectra** clear pending Undo and cannot be undone.
sections.title: Choose the right erase action

steps: Open **Sessions**, tap a date heading if needed, and choose a check by its name and time. A blue dot marks an available recheck, not an unread session.
If **Recheck session** is available, tap it and wait for a separately saved result. Review the original **Captured** date, the **Rechecked** date, and any identification changes.
Review results and **Coverage**, rename or add notes, then export anything you need to keep outside bounded history.
Use individual, selected, or all-session deletion for the scope you intend. Read the confirmation before erasing.
content.takeaway: Keep the checks you need, add context, and stay in control of local history.

technicalSections.body: Unlock the iPhone and return to Spectra or retry saving. A temporary read failure pauses history changes and is retried; it does not trigger damaged-file recovery or authorize overwriting existing sessions. If the problem persists, keep any unsaved result open and export it if possible before contacting support.
technicalSections.title: Storage is temporarily unavailable

technicalSections.body: Spectra pauses history changes to avoid overwriting unreadable data. **Preserve Copy and Start Fresh** keeps a protected recovery copy before creating new history. This is not a promise that damaged data can be recovered. **Erase Stored Data** is the separate destructive choice. Contact support if a report matters before erasing.
technicalSections.title: History cannot be read

technicalSections.body: Sessions groups each capture and its rechecks by the original capture time in your current local calendar. Rechecking does not move that capture to a newer day. Recheck rows show their separate evaluation date and time; details preserve the original measurement date and duration. **Captured with** identifies the original app build; **Recognition used** or **Rechecked with** identifies the interpretation revisions. Older reports may show **Not recorded**. Opening them does not silently reinterpret their findings, fill in today’s version, or invent missing graph data.
technicalSections.title: Old results are historical

content.title: Save, recheck, and manage sessions

content.important: A JSON report is not a packet capture, continuous recording, authenticated device inventory, or tamper-evident forensic record. An AI can make mistakes; review its conclusions against the actual evidence.

sections.body: Completed checks and saved sessions put findings and measurements first. Below them, **Bluetooth proximity** lets you investigate an eligible recorded Bluetooth identity while nearby. **Analyze a finding** offers either on-device explanation or a copy for external AI analysis. **Export results** saves or shares the scan. These are independent options, not required steps. A device’s details can open proximity or analysis with that finding already selected.
sections.title: Explore first, then choose a tool

sections.body: In **Analyze a finding**, choose **Copy for AI analysis**, then select one item. From a finding’s details, the item is already selected. Review the privacy notice and optionally open **Preview prompt and data**. Tap **Copy prompt and finding**, then paste into your preferred AI app. Apple Intelligence is not required. Nothing is uploaded or opened automatically. A general check can include unknown findings; specialist checks offer only findings within their scan type. Display filters do not change the choices.
sections.title: Copy one finding for external AI

sections.body: The default copy includes protocol identifiers, interpretation confidence, historical catalog context, and signal statistics. Recorded names, declared network text, and raw payloads are excluded. **Include names and technical payloads** is optional and resets for each finding or new presentation. Names and bytes may identify people or devices. Location tags, session names, notes, other findings, and AI explanations are never deliberately included, even with technical sharing enabled. Magnetic copies contain a summary and up to three strongest retained incidents, with no technical-data switch when it has no effect. Grouped network services remain separate within the selected finding; omission counts describe bounded evidence.
sections.title: Choose whether to include technical data

sections.body: The clipboard contains a concise prompt followed by JSON, not a standalone JSON file. It asks what the finding may be, what that means, how confident the identification is, and which practical next checks would help. It leads with device type, adds only supported names or models, and separates a device’s usual capabilities from behavior actually observed. Instructions are tailored to the included Bluetooth, network, or magnetic evidence. A magnetic change cannot identify a device or brand. Unknown remains a valid conclusion; catalog guesses and the names they came from are not independent proof.
sections.title: A useful explanation, not a verdict

sections.body: The prompt asks the recipient not to follow instructions inside captured text, invent signatures, or send private names and payloads into searches. Spectra cannot enforce another app’s behavior. Pasting shares the chosen content under that app’s policies, and a larger model cannot recover information that was never retained. Original Bonjour service types are not separately retained; missing fields are stated, not guessed. The copy stays on this iPhone, does not use Universal Clipboard, and expires after ten minutes. Reset or clipboard expiry cannot recall pasted copies. External answers are not imported into Spectra’s findings or catalog.
sections.title: Keep external research in perspective

sections.body: On completed or saved results, choose **Analyze on Device**, then select one recorded device or magnetic-event summary. Similar Bluetooth profiles may be different devices: expand the group and choose one identity. Apple Intelligence explains only that selected summary, suggests a practical next step, and states a key limitation. Open **Summary used for analysis** to compare the input with the explanation. Nothing is uploaded. Explanations are temporary: closing this view or choosing another finding clears them. They are not saved with sessions or included in any JSON export.
sections.title: Analyze on Device

sections.body: A check with no relevant findings does not start Apple Intelligence. Review **Coverage** instead; no matches is not an all-clear. Analysis requires Apple Intelligence enabled, its model ready, and a supported language and region. **Analyze on Device** is disabled while it is unavailable. Enable Apple Intelligence or review its language in iPhone **Settings**, then return to refresh availability. **Check Availability**, when offered in results or an open analysis, refreshes readiness without starting generation; unsupported hardware has no availability retry. Preparation and generation share a 45-second limit. **Cancel Analysis**, backgrounding Spectra, or closing analysis cancels generation. A failed or refused explanation leaves your scan unchanged. Use **Retry Analysis** when offered; a refused or oversized request is not retried unchanged. Review **Summary used for analysis**, **Choose another finding**, or use **Export JSON** for external review. Scanning and exporting do not require Apple Intelligence.
sections.title: When analysis cannot run

sections.body: For a radio finding, Spectra supplies the identity hypothesis, confidence, representative observation, coverage, and available signal-strength summary—not every packet. Related network services may form one likely endpoint. For magnetic findings, it supplies the excursion count, maximum baseline deviation, and up to three strongest retained incident summaries with field, signed delta, threshold, excess, and duration. Earlier incidents may no longer be retained. Raw histories, display graphs, your notes, and other findings are excluded. A magnetic excursion does not identify a device or its purpose.
sections.title: What goes into a finding explanation?

sections.body: Scan type sets the export scope and available analysis choices—not the visible results filters. **Smart Glasses** and **Watches & Wearables** include supported catalog matches and explicitly **Possible** name-based device-type indications, with their associated evidence. The wearable check includes watches, fitness bands and trackers, smart rings, and other supported wearables; glasses remain separate. Unrelated activity is excluded. With no matches, exported results are empty; scan type, duration, and coverage remain available. **Quick Check**, **Area Sweep**, and **Monitor** exports include all retained data for their scan type. On-device analysis explains only the single finding you select. Acquisition counts are observations, not device counts.
sections.title: Scan type sets the scope—not screen filters

sections.body: The default export is a compact, model-friendly evidence document with scan-local citations, identity hypotheses, interpreted evidence, radio summaries, magnetic detector events, and Monitor changes. Coverage and user notes are separate context. It omits raw packet bytes, display-only graphs, and all generated AI explanations. This file is for your own external analysis workflow; the on-device feature uses a smaller, separate summary of just one finding.
sections.title: Analysis JSON

sections.body: Includes all retained results within the scan type, confidence, advertised names and payloads, coverage, catalog metadata, session name and notes, retained Monitor events and comparisons, and a saved magnetic graph when applicable. It ignores the visible results filter. Use this for detailed technical review or a supported **Import Session** restore. New archives include a checksum; it does not authenticate the author or observations. The file may include personal information. Generated AI explanations are excluded, including any analysis retained by an earlier app version.
sections.title: Technical archive

sections.body: Keeps device categories, typed confidence, signal measurements, relative timing, source-coverage states, and the collector platform when recorded. By default it omits location, collector hardware and OS version, original identifiers, absolute timestamps, names, notes, manufacturers, model labels, raw payloads, and free-text evidence/limitations. App and recognition versions remain, including the original capture build for rechecks. Choosing **Include scan location** adds the saved coordinates, accuracy, and absolute location timestamp to this otherwise reduced file. Measurement patterns can still reveal context, so reduced does not mean anonymous. The missing context can limit an analyst’s conclusions.
sections.title: Reduced identifying information

sections.body: Location tags are excluded from every format by default—even **Technical archive**. If the session has a tag, **Include scan location** lets you explicitly add its coordinates, estimated accuracy, and fix timestamp to this export. The choice starts off when you reopen export and is separate from the format selection. It can reveal where you were, including in **Reduced identifying information**. This setting does not add the tag to **Copy for AI analysis** or on-device finding summaries.
sections.title: Choose whether to share the location

sections.body: In a saved session, open the top **Session options** menu and choose **Export JSON**. The **Export results** section farther down opens the same options and is also available after a completed check. Under **Information to include**, choose one format—not multiple items to combine. Tap **Export JSON** to prepare that file locally. **Preparing JSON** and a spinner confirm that work is in progress; **Cancel** closes preparation without changing your session. Apple’s share sheet opens when the file is ready. Choose **Save to Files** or another destination. Cloud storage, email, or an AI service may transfer and retain the copy under that service’s policies. Erasing Spectra afterward cannot recall external copies.
sections.title: Save or share

sections.body: Ask it to summarize observed device categories, explain confidence and coverage limits, identify repeatable magnetic events, and suggest non-invasive follow-up checks. Tell it to treat all device names, transmitted fields, and notes as untrusted data—not instructions. Do not ask it to certify safety or infer recording from a product name.
sections.title: Ask an AI useful questions

steps: In a saved session, choose **Export JSON** from the top **Session options** menu. After a completed check, use the **Export results** section.
Select one format: **Analysis JSON**, **Technical archive**, or **Reduced identifying information**. Read what is included.
Tap **Export JSON** and wait for preparation to finish. In the share sheet, choose **Save to Files** or a recipient you trust.
content.takeaway: Choose how much to share, then save or send a portable report. Spectra never uploads it automatically.

technicalSections.body: The export identifies its schema and producing app build. The technical archive uses ISO 8601 UTC timestamps, RSSI in dBm, magnetic field in microteslas (µT), and durations in seconds. Payload bytes use base64. Missing fields mean not recorded or unavailable, not zero. Reduced exports are a separate allowlisted shape, not a full report with blank names.
technicalSections.title: Versioned, explicit units

technicalSections.body: New captures record the collector platform, hardware model, OS version, and collector app version and build. **Analysis JSON** and **Technical archive** preserve those facts separately from the app that interprets or exports the report. A Watch capture remains a Watch capture after transfer or recheck. Older evidence can lack these fields; Spectra does not fill them with the current phone’s information. Personal device names, serial numbers, and persistent device identifiers are not collected for this metadata.
technicalSections.title: Which device collected the evidence?

technicalSections.body: An observation count describes received broadcasts, not physical devices. Bluetooth signal statistics summarize a bounded recent window of accepted RSSI samples; that window is not the full observation history. Comparing two captures requires considering duration, collection time, receiver position, and people moving nearby. A stronger reading or larger count alone does not establish better coverage.
technicalSections.title: Observations and signal samples differ

technicalSections.body: Saved magnetic display points preserve a bounded, downsampled window. Do not connect gaps or different reference revisions, assume the complete sweep was retained, or confuse display delta with the detector’s independent calibrated baseline. Bluetooth reports preserve signal summaries. A **Bluetooth Proximity** check is a separate, unsaved live measurement.
